checks.name: Stance-rule justification
checks.evidence: Requiring the pooled per-stance sampling error (90th-percentile per-stance sd 0.047 log divided by the square root of n) to be at most the calibration sd (0.0152) gives n ≥ (0.047/0.0152)^2 = 9.56 (the handoff says 9.7, presumably from an unrounded 0.047; immaterial). This is sound as a heuristic, assuming stance errors are independent. I confirmed from the screen records that matched trials have either 4 stances (10 trials) or at least 11, so any threshold from 5 to 11 gives the same split. The rule is post hoc, which the audit states (post_hoc true, set after my round-1 finding), and it only removes trials.

round_1.summary: The census is applied as recorded. I recomputed all 488 classes, candidate sets and factors from the recorded estimates with my own implementation of rules{} and got 0 mismatches; the 23-trial fragile set reproduces exactly; the census code hash 0d96b700 reproduces when the sensitivity stage is removed. 'Unreliable' is not too conservative: on non-gait trials, equally plausible mass-free estimators disagree by up to 7 %, and the mass table is too dense for any ±5 % method. The knee power ratio is explained: published powers use the 6 Hz low-passed moment (ratio 1.0000, corr 1.0000). checks.name: Own-code sample, seed 20261104 (23 trials) + 8 exact calibration trials
checks.result: pass (census reproduced) with one robustness finding
checks.evidence: Sample stratified by the worker's classes (frame read from the audit): 6 unique-estimate, 5 ambiguous, 2 no-match, 6 non-gait unreliable, 1 not-usable stairs, 1 curb, 1 low-corr. Estimators (mass-free, Virtual_Insoles): e1 = gait stances with a fixed talus point; e2 = talus point fitted with the mass, all loaded samples; e3 = fixed talus, all loaded samples. On the 8 exact trials: e1 bias 1.043 (robust sd 0.026), e2 1.004 (sd 0.012, worst -3.0 % AB13 and +4.3 % AB10), e3 1.047 (sd 0.020). e2 is about as well calibrated as the worker's estimator (bias 0.994, sd 0.015). Gait classes, worker lever vs my e2/1.004: AB05 turn_and_step_1 113.5 vs 112.0 (same unique 113.5, AB03's); ambiguous trials stay ambiguous (AB08 obstacle 61.2 vs 63.3; AB12 obstacle 65.8 vs 65.4; AB12 stairs_1_7 65.2 vs 64.9; AB13 side_shuffle 61.9 vs 63.5). Robustness finding: of 6 sampled unique-estimates, only AB05 turn_and_step_1 stays unique with the same mass under e2. AB07 side_shuffle_1 (11 stances, fragile) moves to 71.5 (factor 1.148 instead of 1.266; split halves 76.6/68.2). AB07 weighted_walk_1 (fragile), AB09 stairs_1_4 (fragile) and AB09 stairs_1_9 (well-separated, 4 stances) become ambiguous. AB08 stairs_1_5 (well-separated, 4 stances, factor 0.711, the census minimum) has no table mass within 4.9 % under e2 (57.6 kg). The worker's divisor lies within ±4.9 % of my e2 in 4 of 6, so assignment is consistent on balance, but uniqueness is estimator-dependent in short or unstable trials. Of the 38 well-separated trials, 4 are 4-stance stairs trials. No-match AB09 dynamic_walk_1 / weighted_walk_1 (worker 92.4 / 92.0): e2 gives 87.6 / 88.4 (split halves 97.0 / 87.3 unstable, and 89.1 / 88.4). Both are probably AB08's 87.6 read 5 % high by the fixed-talus estimator; 'no-match' is conservative and harmless.

checks.name: Is 'unreliable' too conservative? Alternative methods for non-gait
checks.evidence: Non-gait trials give high correlations (0.994-0.9993), but the estimators disagree. AB02 poses_1: e2 77.3 vs e3 86.7/1.047 = 82.8 kg (7 % apart; candidates 78.9 / 79.1 / 82.2 / 84.1). AB01 ball_toss_1 e2 split halves 79.9 / 76.3 (4.7 %). AB12 lunges_1: e1 / e2 / e3 bias-corrected 76.8 / 79.6 / 76.5. AB06 jump_2: e2 69.5 sits between 67.6 and 71.5. No exact reference exists outside normal_walk_1 to decide which estimator is right in quasi-static postures. In quiet stance the CoP is near the talus, the configuration most sensitive to talus-position error. Vertical GRF vs body weight re-measures body mass (already verified correct) and carries no information on the moment divisor. A known-reference-trial transfer assumes the divisor is constant within a subject, which the census disproves (AB05, AB07, AB01, AB06, AB10, AB13). The mass table is dense: within ±4.9 %, every table mass except 71.5 and 113.5 has 1-4 neighbours (for example 65.1: 62.3, 64.0, 67.5, 67.6). So even a perfect non-gait estimator at ±2-3 % would leave most trials ambiguous. Conclusion: 'unreliable' reflects missing calibration and an intrinsic resolution limit. A different method would need its own exact reference, which does not exist here.

checks.name: Class rules and fragile rule
checks.evidence: My own implementation of rules{} on the recorded lever divisors, families, stance counts and correlations gives the same class for 488/488 trials, the same candidate sets, and the same rescale factors (|diff| < 0.001). Unreliable reasons: non-gait 196, not usable 76, curb 24, corr < 0.98 7. The 8 exact divisors equal the C03 re-run values; AB09 87.57 maps to 87.6 under the 0.1 % rule. Fragile rule: added after the census (sensitivity.added_after_census true; it reads only the audit). Recomputed from the recorded divisors it gives the same 23 trials. It only splits unique-estimate into two groups and changes no class or factor, so it is post hoc but harmless. Removing the sensitivity function and its two argparse lines reproduces the census code sha256 0d96b700... recorded in the audit. rules_fixed_at_utc (18:27:21) is from the final run (finished 18:28:52), so it shows ordering within that run only; the honesty note covers the pilots and the power-rule change.

checks.name: Knee power ratio 0.83-1.03
checks.evidence: Published Joint_Powers = [5th-order zero-lag Butterworth 6 Hz low-pass of Joint_Moments] x Joint_Velocities (rad/s). Median ratio 1.0000, slope 1.000, corr 1.0000 in all 12 knee/ankle columns of AB05 side_shuffle_1 (the census minimum, raw knee 0.83/0.87), AB01 incline_walk_2 and AB05 meander_1. It also equals ProcessedData moment_filt x velocity exactly (ratio 1.0000, corr 1.0000) for side_shuffle_1 and meander_1. Against the raw moment the knee reads 0.83-0.98, because the knee moment carries high-frequency content (impact peaks) that the filter removes. The ankle moment is smooth (about 0.99-1.00), and slow overground tasks give about 1.00 (consistent with the audit's family pattern). Consequences: the filter is linear, so each trial's moment divisor applies to hip, knee and ankle powers equally, and powers can take the same rescale factor. The worker's power check could include the knee by using the filtered moment. RawData powers are not raw-moment x velocity, which belongs in the GT23 documentation.

checks.name: Decision D-GT23-C04-1

Options are ordered neutrally by trials released (0, 38, 61), stated in options_order; decide_before_recommendation is true. B's consequence calls the 38 'well separated' without saying that 4 are 4-stance stairs trials whose match changes under an equally calibrated estimator (check 1). The check field is accurate: 75.2 kg is 4.7 % below 78.9 and 5.2 % above 71.5.
